historical_reviews.deepseek: Package dependency is relevant; its injection command, destructive risk and error-log oracle are a testcase mismatch.

original_test_intent: Enumerate the AMD GPU RAS devices/features exposed by amdgpuras and confirm that the target MI300-family configuration reports the complete owner-approved Device list.
original_method: Identify GPU UUID/BDF/model, driver/firmware/OS and amdgpuras build; capture `sudo amdgpuras -l` stdout/stderr and exit status; separately filter Device lines without treating the filter as complete evidence; compare every entry and count with the approved platform inventory; preserve diagnostics if discovery fails.
manual_activity: The platform owner provides the supported amdgpuras build and expected per-GPU Device/feature inventory; the agent performs the read-only listing and returns the comparison evidence.
required_inputs: Compatible AMDGPU-RAS amdgpuras package, version/build provenance and installation approval if absent
Target GPU UUID, PCIe BDF, model and confirmation whether CHIP_AQUA_VANJARAM naming is expected
Driver, firmware, kernel and OS supported combination
Expected Device entry names, count and ordering/duplication rules for every installed accelerator
Approved interpretation of unsupported, missing or unexpected entries
safety_requirements: Use only `-l` discovery and the literal read-only filter; reject any mutation or injection flags
Do not unload/reload drivers, reset GPUs, clear logs or disturb active workloads for this case
Capture full output before filtering so non-Device warnings and unsupported-hardware messages remain visible
Bind output to current UUID/BDF inventory and package version
Stop if sudo resolves to an unexpected binary or the tool indicates an unsupported GPU
agent_execution_scope: Verify binary path/version, GPU identity and expected inventory
Run `sudo amdgpuras -l` and `sudo amdgpuras -l | grep -i "Device"`, preserving stdout/stderr/status
Compare output without installing unapproved packages or modifying driver/GPU state; do not inject, reset or decide DUT PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve amdgpuras build and expected Device/feature matrix
Resolve codename, unsupported-hardware or inventory discrepancies
Issue the final verdict from the captured comparison

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not applicable: it proposes injection success and hardware-error dmesg evidence although the source only lists device features.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After package and expected-list confirmation, run the two literal `amdgpuras -l` commands and compare the complete output to the approved per-GPU inventory.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: `sudo amdgpuras -l`, the Device filter, MI300 codename note, Common branch and 5/5-minute estimates are preserved exactly; no injection is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform read-only enumeration with complete-output capture and an explicit UUID/BDF-to-expected-feature comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds tool provenance, stable GPU identity, full-output retention and a measurable expected matrix while retaining the literal commands.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The source's phrase 'list correctly' cannot be evaluated without an expected inventory; filtered lines alone can also hide tool warnings.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Package mismatch or codename differences can create false inventory failures, but no hardware fault should be generated.

project_override_considerations: Use the project-approved MI300 family/device naming and tool build. Do not infer expected devices solely from the CHIP_AQUA_VANJARAM note or from GPU index order.
expected_evidence: amdgpuras resolved path, version/build/checksum or approved package provenance
Full `amdgpuras -l` stdout/stderr, exit status and filtered Device lines
Expected-versus-observed entry-by-entry and count comparison for each target GPU
Relevant dmesg/tool diagnostics only if discovery fails; no injected-error evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe a read-only list operation. The mismatch is in DeepSeek's derived review, not the protected source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Purpose and commands are explicit. Package availability and expected inventory are normal execution prerequisites, so static review completes without BLOCKED classification.

review_improvement: Removes the erroneous injection path and converts vague correctness into a package-, identity- and expected-inventory-based read-only comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: The `-l` option enumerates tool-visible features and contains no source-specified injection selector. Therefore an 'Error inject successfully' message or hardware-error dmesg line would indicate the wrong operation, not stronger evidence. Full output and stable UUID/BDF identity are necessary because a grep can omit warnings and GPU indices may change.
